text.inkscape:label: THREE GROUNDS
text.tspan: The hospital didn't close. It changed patient.
Its courtyards, tunnels, kitchens and walls now care for the city — its loneliness, its segregations,
its weather, its restless young. Public life occupies three inhabited layers: a basement city of
culture reached through new daylight wells; a ground city of courtyards, portico and civic square;
a sky city of retrofitted balconies, rooftop dwellings around winter gardens, and a public crown.
Programmes overlap by design, so the neighbourhood breathes through every hour.
The former Odense University Hospital does not need to be replaced. It needs to be redirected.
The hospital's care infrastructure, its courtyards, its tunnels, its kitchens, its 1912 brick pavilions,
and its 1967 tower, stays. Only the patient changes.
The new patient is the city: lonely, segregated, weather exposed, and uncertain of its commons.
Public life occupies three inhabited layers, connected by lifts, stairs, water, and planting. The
basement city, formed by the existing tunnel network and Building 01's basements, becomes the
cultural city, housing cinemas, a music venue, a climbing wall, a skate bowl, a market, a sauna,
and electric mobility, all brought daylight through the existing courtyards that already descend
to basement level. The ground city, shaped by heritage courtyards, the new portico beneath the
tower's social balconies, the civic square along the north, and the western stepwell, becomes the
pedestrian and planted commons. The sky city, formed by retrofitted balconies on the existing
towers with social nodes and access galleries, rooftop dwellings above deep plan halls arranged
around winter garden courtyards, and a public crown, becomes the place where homes meet daylight
The neighbourhood serves those Danish urban regeneration has historically left to the side: women
led cooking commons, women only sauna hours, the rolling commons, not a boys' skate park,
intergenerational childcare, and accessible single floor homes for elderly women and single mothers,
alongside lit night routes for safe walking and running.
Programmes overlap rather than separate into zones. The community canteen is a café at 06:00, a
public canteen at midday, and an event space in the evening. The Long Room becomes commute,
market, promenade, and lit colonnade in turn. The Sharing Factory works by day and rehearses by
night. Buildings remain alive in shifts.
The retrofit standard is not speculative. Building 09 already achieves A2010 energy rating within
heritage SAVE 2 constraints, and its ground floor opens as the project's Manifesto Building, making
proof public. International precedent is translated through approximately 50 speaker portraits located
in specific buildings, synthetic testimonies that triangulate Danish survey data with global research
and are extracted as design constraints. Speculative, sourced, and declared.
The rhizome is not a metaphor. It is a safety strategy. Where the network surfaces, at every well,
every threshold, every roof stair, and every named place, the city offers a choice. Choice is what
safety means for those who have rarely been given any.
Safety is infrastructure and isnot policing.
Beneath the city lies the well of care. The work of those who came before us is in the ground. We tend
it daily, and what grows from it is what the city makes of itself.
